newsitem.title: USA: Provident American to post Q2 loss.
newsitem.headline: Provident American to post Q2 loss.

text.p: Provident American Corp said on Tuesday that it will post a second quarter loss in the second quarter after it increased reserves in the range of $3 million to $5 million.
The company increased reserves because it expects a greater than expected loss ratio associated with higher out of network use by policyholers of its Solution health care plan, Provident said.
Provident said it expects to report sequential operating earnings for the second half of 1997 and increased profitability for 1998.
After this adjustment, the company's capital will exceed its risk based capital requirements.
"Recent developments indicated higher than expected loss ratios for our lower deductible and managed care plans," president and chief operating officer Jim Bowles said in a statement.

Provident said it has begun implementing more aggressive price increases for its lower deductible plans and changed its managed care plans so policy holders pay more when they are treated by doctors and hospitals outside the HealthCare COMPARE Corp network.

The company said it intends to boost use of the healthcare network to more than 85 percent from the present 50 percent. Provident said initial pricing of the plan was based on 80 percent use of the network.
Provident receives discounts up to 40 percent when its insureds use doctors and hospitals within HealthCare COMPARE's network, it said.
